shortcut_name: two-protocol complement reduces every link to a bipartite inequality
evidence: deepseek uses "color = [-1] * n" and BFS with "color[v] = color[u] ^ 1"; gpt-oss uses "color = [-1] * n # 0 / 1 during BFS"; glm likewise initializes "color = [-1] * n" and performs graph traversal
affordance_in_statement: The available protocol suite consists of exactly two protocols, designated 1 and 2. The protocol not chosen by tower i automatically becomes its inactive backup protocol. ... the primary active protocol of tower u must exactly match the inactive backup protocol of tower v.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: with exactly two protocols and the other protocol forced as backup, matching an endpoint's backup is inherently equivalent to requiring different endpoint assignments. Removing it would require changing the protocol domain, backup rule, or adding another constraint.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes each link as an opposite-color constraint and solves the graph by BFS two-coloring, then chooses the component orientation for the lexicographically smallest assignment.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The protocol not chosen by tower i automatically becomes its inactive backup protocol, combined with exactly two protocols.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses 0/1 BFS coloring of each connected component and component orientation to construct the lexicographically smallest valid assignment.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The primary active protocol must exactly match the other endpoint's inactive backup protocol.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Performs standard DFS/BFS bipartite coloring using the binary protocol choices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The available protocol suite consists of exactly two protocols, designated 1 and 2.

common_affordance: Because there are exactly two protocols and the unchosen one is forced as backup, every critical link is simply the constraint f_u != f_v, so the task is graph bipartiteness plus component orientation.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Timed out because its implementation did not complete its graph processing and/or lexicographic construction within the limit; this is an implementation-efficiency failure rather than a failure to identify the bipartite reduction.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors because the binary-complement reduction is the intrinsic task. If changing the task is allowed while preserving the input/output formats, append a global condition such as requiring exactly floor(n/2) towers to use protocol 1; this makes component orientation alone insufficient and defeats the submitted solutions.
regression_risk: The added global condition could accidentally make the already-TLE qwen3-coder solution pass only on small or specially balanced cases; otherwise it should not restore any defeated model.
